chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: Studying arranging and theory in New York
summary: Horace began arranging on his own; the Schillinger system was a fad among Fletcher's men, and he enrolled for theory and harmony with Damrosch but did not stay.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Okay. Were the arrangements that you were using at that time, were they still a lot of them ones that Fletcher had given you, or were you writing your own?
I had begun to kind of go out on my own, and I began to study a few things, and I went to school a little bit in New York.
Where did you go, or -- how did you study, what did you study?

You know, I studied a little bit arranging, but they had the different systems in New York, you know -- excuse me -- it got to be a fad around there with the guys. My brother had a trumpet player named Dick Vance, and there was certain systems there, the Schillinger system, Eddie Barefield, (unintelligible) the great lead saxophonist, you know, he played with Fletcher, too. They all went to school and studied this system so I got in on this. I first had enrolled at Walter Damrosch (unintelligible), studying theory and harmony, (unintelligible) Solfegeio.
Did you work with him personally?

I started to school there, but I didn't stay. I was -- I played in Long Island and the commuting during that time was bad. I was -- there's a place -- have you ever heard of a place called Jones Beach?
